This is an excellent opportunity to gain experience, learn, and develop your career within the automotive industry. jobs.title: Service Technician - 2nd Shift - Tysons Galleria
jobs.description_text: As a Service Technician , you will be responsible for diagnosing, maintaining and repairing Lucid Motors vehicles. You will demonstrate your passion for sustainable transportation and creatively solve problems in a fast-paced environment. As a Service Technician, it is expected to have ASE certifications obtained within 6-8 months of hire date. Lucid will reimburse the cost associated with successful completion. Responsibilities: Confidently repair basic and major mechanical issues and perform basic electrical and mechanical diagnosis Maintain a high knowledge level of High Voltage (HV), Low Voltage (LV), and general electric vehicle systems Follow correct repair order documentation procedures, i.e. The Three C's Effectively work with the appropriate software suite to properly and completely document all customer vehicle interactions Effectively communicate and collaborate with other members of the service team (i.e., advisor, manager, etc.) as well as customers. Ability to demonstrate and teach learned technical skills/knowledge with others Demonstrate attention to detail and passion for creating positive client experiences Ability to work remotely and support mobile service team as needed Other duties as assigned Qualifications: 2-5 years of experience as an automotive service technician, including previous experience with EV/HEV diagnosis and repair Knowledge of High Voltage systems, Low Voltage systems, and Electric Vehicle powertrains Customer facing experience exhibitin

jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Strategic Defense builds the command and control and fire control software for integrated air and missile defense. We work the hard end of the problem: ballistic missiles, hypersonic glide vehicles, cruise missiles, and saturation raids that arrive faster than any human-paced decision cycle can absorb. The US air and missile defense enterprise was assembled over four decades, one program at a time. Army air defense runs on one battle manager, short range air defense on another, the ballistic missile defense system on a third, and the fleet on a fourth. Each of them was engineered well for the threat it was scoped against. None of them was designed to be extended by anyone other than the prime that built it, which is why adding a sensor or an effector to an existing architecture is still a multi-year integration program rather than a software release. That is the opening we are working. A software-defined fire control layer, built on Lattice, with interfaces open enough that a new sensor, a new interceptor, or a new effects chain can be brought in at the pace software moves rather than the pace a hardware program moves. The technical case is strong and the early programs are real. What we need now is someone who can turn that into share inside programs of record.
